questions.q: According to the article, what did the Prophet seek to gain by agreeing to the Treaty of Hudaybiya on his opponents’ terms?
options: Time to prepare a larger army
Not quite. The article says: Peace itself, for the opportunities it opens – justice is then reached by using those opportunities.
An immediate and complete settlement of every claim
Not quite. The article says: Peace itself, for the opportunities it opens – justice is then reached by using those opportunities.
Peace itself, for the opportunities it opens – justice is then reached by using those opportunities
Yes. “God grants to peace what He does not grant to violence.”
The goodwill of neighbouring kings
Not quite. The article says: Peace itself, for the opportunities it opens – justice is then reached by using those opportunities.
questions.rationale: “Justice does not come from peace itself; peace creates opportunities, and justice is achieved by utilizing them.”

questions.q: Hearing many people tell of injustices done to them, what question occurred to the author?
options: If everyone claims to be the victim, who is the oppressor?
Right. Each was shifting his own mistakes onto others.
Who was the richest among them?
Not quite. The article says: If everyone claims to be the victim, who is the oppressor?.
Why had they not moved elsewhere?
Not quite. The article says: If everyone claims to be the victim, who is the oppressor?.
Why were the courts not helping them?
Not quite. The article says: If everyone claims to be the victim, who is the oppressor?.
questions.rationale: “I wondered, if everyone claimed to be a victim, who was playing the oppressor? Eventually, I realized that each person was shifting their mistakes onto others.”

questions.q: What does the article say happens once a person takes ownership of his own part in a problem?
options: Problems begin to resolve, and he grows more thoughtful and mature
Yes. Change begins by looking inward.
Nothing changes
Not quite. The article says: Problems begin to resolve, and he grows more thoughtful and mature.
Others take advantage of him
Not quite. The article says: Problems begin to resolve, and he grows more thoughtful and mature.
The problem grows larger
Not quite. The article says: Problems begin to resolve, and he grows more thoughtful and mature.
questions.rationale: “Once you take ownership of your role in issues, problems seem to resolve almost effortlessly.”

questions.q: What flaw does the article find in the argument that natural causes make belief in God unnecessary?
options: Scientists disagree about gravity
Not quite. The article says: Finding a cause for an event does not explain why the causes themselves exist.
Finding a cause for an event does not explain why the causes themselves exist
Well reasoned. The question of ultimate origin remains.
Science has found very few causes
Not quite. The article says: Finding a cause for an event does not explain why the causes themselves exist.
Natural causes do not really exist
Not quite. The article says: Finding a cause for an event does not explain why the causes themselves exist.
questions.rationale: “The existence of a natural cause does not preclude the need for an ultimate explanation… causes themselves require explanation.”

Religious scholars

Governments

Newton and the first scientists

questions.q: Abu Hurairah narrated thousands of Hadiths, while Khalid bin Al-Waleed was known for courage in the field. What does the article draw from the difference?
options: Each person has distinct God-given abilities and serves best by recognising and using his own
Yes. A “silent covenant” with the Creator.
Everyone should aim at the same role
Not quite. The article says: Each person has distinct God-given abilities and serves best by recognising and using his own.
One was more devoted than the other
Not quite. The article says: Each person has distinct God-given abilities and serves best by recognising and using his own.
Memory matters more than courage
Not quite. The article says: Each person has distinct God-given abilities and serves best by recognising and using his own.
questions.rationale: “This distinction was not about their dedication to Islam but about their natural abilities and the fields in which they excelled.”

questions.q: What does the article say should decide who is given a responsibility?
options: Who asks first
Not quite. The article says: Merit and expertise in that work, not seniority or personal ties.
Friendship with the leaders
Not quite. The article says: Merit and expertise in that work, not seniority or personal ties.
Length of service
Not quite. The article says: Merit and expertise in that work, not seniority or personal ties.
Merit and expertise in that work, not seniority or personal ties

questions.article: The Creative Study of the Quran
questions.q: What test does Maulana give for knowing whether one has truly embraced the Quran?
options: How finely it is printed
Not quite. The article says: Whether it has sparked fresh, creative thinking through daily reflection.
How many times one has finished reading it
Not quite. The article says: Whether it has sparked fresh, creative thinking through daily reflection.
Whether it has sparked fresh, creative thinking through daily reflection
Yes. Not memorised translations.
How much of it one can recite
Not quite. The article says: Whether it has sparked fresh, creative thinking through daily reflection.
questions.rationale: “The test to know if you have embraced the Quran is whether it has sparked creative thinking in you.”

questions.q: The Arabic word shahada means “witnessing.” What does the article conclude about the true meaning of martyrdom?
options: Winning as many battles as possible
Not quite. The article says: Living as a witness to truth and peace – living for a cause, not seeking death.
Seeking death in battle
Not quite. The article says: Living as a witness to truth and peace – living for a cause, not seeking death.
Living as a witness to truth and peace – living for a cause, not seeking death
Exactly. The Prophet chose the trench and the treaty.
Withdrawing from the world
Not quite. The article says: Living as a witness to truth and peace – living for a cause, not seeking death.
questions.rationale: “The ultimate form of martyrdom is living for a cause, not dying for it.”

questions.q: What two levels of conduct does the article describe for a member of society?
options: At the least, causing no harm to anyone; at the highest, being a source of benefit to others
Well read. “The best among you are those who bring the most benefit to others.”
Obeying the law; and avoiding people
Not quite. The article says: At the least, causing no harm to anyone; at the highest, being a source of benefit to others.
Earning well; and spending well
Not quite. The article says: At the least, causing no harm to anyone; at the highest, being a source of benefit to others.
Speaking little; and travelling much
Not quite. The article says: At the least, causing no harm to anyone; at the highest, being a source of benefit to others.
questions.rationale: “If one cannot offer a direct benefit to others, they should make it their duty to avoid causing harm.”
